title: Every IFC file has one fixed shape: an IfcProject root with six branches
content:
Analysis of three different IFC files yields one universal working model. One root object (**IfcProject**), then six branches:

- **spatial** — Site › Building › Storey › Space
- **elements** — physical objects, grouped by class
- **properties** — property sets, and how much of each is genuinely filled
- **process** — tasks, dependencies, schedule windows
- **issues** — BCF topics; these always live *outside* the IFC and join back by GlobalId
- **relations** — the typed edges holding the graph together

What changes between files is which branches carry data: a design export fills spatial and elements and leaves process empty; a 4D planning export fills process. The shape stays put while the contents change.

This is the conceptual snapshot that makes IFC files accessible to LLMs — e.g. "this file has one building with one floor and two rooms with IDs …" — and it is the foundation of the dtbau demo's Source 1 (IFC object hierarchy extraction).
description: IFC files share one structure — IfcProject root, then spatial, elements, properties, process, issues, relations. Files differ only in which branches carry data.
